Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\n\\n[Run 1 of 2 \\u00B7 84030b56]\\n\\n- What now exists: \\u0060StackReplayOntoResolver\\u0060 (src/Hall9k.Daemon/Execution/StackReplayOntoResolver.cs), wired into \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060\\u0027s StackReplay dispatch path, plus a new prompt fragment and three new/updated test files.\\n- Non-obvious shape: \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumberer\\u0060 needed no code change. Careful tracing of the actual git topology through the incident (placeholder inherited by both sides, one side\\u0027s assignment staying local until its own gate passed) showed its existing \\u0022declined only if taken at the fork point\\u0022 check already handles this collision correctly; the retry landing short of main\\u0027s true tip (the RunLauncher bug) was the entire root cause. Don\\u0027t re-litigate that decline logic without re-deriving this trace first.\\n- Left as-is, deliberately: \\u0060FollowUpKind.Rebase\\u0060 was checked for the same staleness hazard and doesn\\u0027t have it (its onto target is always a live \\u0060origin/\\u003Cbase\\u003E\\u0060 ref, never a frozen commit), so no resolver was built for it. \\u0060RetryPending\\u0060 is used as the \\u0022is this a retry\\u0022 signal even though it\\u0027s broader than \\u0022this exact relaunch\\u0022 (it stays true until the task ends), which is intentional: recomputing fresh costs nothing and is strictly safer than trusting a value this task has already shown can go stale.\\n\\n[Run 2 of 2 \\u00B7 86fe711a]\\n\\n- What exists now: \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumberer.cs\\u0060 has two bug fixes folded into commit \\u00607806eca0\\u0060 (formerly \\u0060886c4fd7\\u0060): the \\u0060UnreadableCommit\\u0060 guard now covers the placement-note retry shape, and \\u0060TailEntryCarriesOwnPlacementNote\\u0060 matches the mechanically generated note wording instead of a bare marker substring. Two new regression tests cover both fixes in \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumbererTransitionTests.cs\\u0060. All three Copilot threads are resolved on the PR with substantive replies; a top-level PR comment answers the review\\u0027s body, including the suppressed em-dash nit.\\n- Gotcha for whoever picks this up next: this PR branch is now stale against origin/main by 6 commits, including one that independently claimed Decisions Log #199 for a different entry \\u2014 the same number this branch\\u0027s own tail entry already holds locally. Short term: a relay server anyone can stand up per project (and a node can stand one up for its own shared work) that carries the messages and shared state a team needs; long term: those relays become part of a broader peer-to-peer network so a new node or project joins and benefits without infrastructure. Design the relay so the peer-to-peer layer replaces the transport, not the boundary. The immediate driver is the ARX platform\\u0027s .NET Core migration, a strangler-fig port one MVC route, controller, or action at a time, where QA runs ahead of engineering writing baseline end-to-end tests per route and then validates each port before and after; QA needs Hall9k on their machines, and the coordination has to run through Hall9k rather than around it. Today two nodes talk through comments on a private GitHub issue, which works for one person and not for a team. Short term: a relay server anyone can stand up per project (and a node can stand one up for its own shared work) that carries the messages and shared state a team needs; long term: those relays become part of a broader peer-to-peer network so a new node or project joins and benefits without infrastructure. Design the relay so the peer-to-peer layer replaces the transport, not the boundary. This umbrella consolidates the tracker-as-substrate MVP (64c75e43, largely shipped: claim gate, take in tracker, issue carries the task record), the node mailbox prototype and its open questions (notes/node-mailbox.md), the container node with peer-managed nodes (efe71721), the QA-in-the-loop ideas (4e670c74, 21ddf2b3), and the backlog documents backlog/p2p/PLAN-additions.md, backlog/p2p/P2P-KICKOFF-PROMPT.md, backlog/IDEA-p2p-lazy-sync.md, and backlog/IDEA-per-project-store.md with 64e4ebd2\\u0027s database-as-room model.\\n\\nIdea 202383dc (Hall9k for a distributed team). PR #379\\u0027s description disclosed this as a deliberate scope limit and named the fix as project-scoped stream ids in the message feature.
